newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends touch weaker in quiet session.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends touch weaker in quiet session.

text.p: COMEX copper ended slightly weaker after a lackluster rangebound session as the market eased back following the week's advance, but remained well underpinned physically in the United States, dealers said.
July COMEX settled 0.20 cent weaker at 119.25 cents a lb, traded 119.75 to 118.50 cents. Spot June went out 0.10 cent lower at 118.90 cents.

Brokers and merchants expected the market to remain at around this level through June, as LME stocks fell and time was needed for Kennecott Utah Copper to crank up output after its large smelter was fired up on Tuesday after a 42-day shutdown.
"The market in the Northeast is very tight," a merchant said. Premiums on cathode over spot COMEX in the region were strong at 3.25 to 3.75 cents per pound due to the local tightness, he added.
But from July on, the market usually feels a seasonal slowdown, traders cautioned.

Following the run-up in COMEX copper prices, scrap has become more plentiful, but discounts to COMEX spot on key grades used to substitute cathode, have widened to dampen the effect of the stronger cathode prices, a scrap dealer said.
"The scrap is coming out from under the rocks. People felt there was more risk on the downside than on the upside at these prices," the dealer said.
LME stocks fell 3,550 tonnes to 133,025 tonnes on Thursday.

The liquidation of Cerro Sales positions ahead of the company's takeover by MG from June 1, was largely over by Thursday morning, floor sources said. The selloff helped to push spot June into contango over July despite LME cash to three months still in backwardation, the floor sources said.
